text: Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars!
Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the mighty trees are ruined! Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the impenetrable forest has been felled!
Listen—the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is ruined. Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the lush thickets of the Jordan are laid waste.

versions.text: Listen—the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is ruined. Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the thickets of the Jordan are laid waste.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew גְּאוֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן literally means "the pride/majesty of the Jordan," an expression for the dense growth along the river. Adding a qualifier such as "lush" (or a footnote noting the literal sense "the pride of the Jordan") preserves the imagery of splendour being destroyed, which parallels "their glory is ruined" in the first half of the verse.

versions.text: Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the lush thickets of the Jordan are laid waste.
versions.explanation: The entire first half of the verse (קוֹל יִלְלַת הָרֹעִים כִּי שֻׁדְּדָה אַדַּרְתָּם, "the sound of the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is ruined") has dropped out. Restoring it also recovers the deliberate parallelism with the second half and the link back to the wailing of verse 2. The qualifier "lush" from the previous revision is retained.

text: This is what the LORD my God says: Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished, and those who sell them say, "Blessed be the LORD, I have grown rich!" And their own shepherds show them no pity.

For I will no longer show pity to the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD. I will hand everyone over, each to his neighbor and to his king; they will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hand.
So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs: one I called Favor, the other I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
In a single month I destroyed the three shepherds. I grew impatient with them, and they also loathed me.
Then I said, "I will not shepherd you any longer. Let the dying die, let the perishing perish, and let those who remain devour one another's flesh."
Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, annulling the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
It was annulled that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that this was the word of the LORD.
Then I said to them, "If it seems right to you, pay me my wages; if not, keep them." So they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter"—that noble price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty shekels of silver and threw the money into the house of the LORD, to the potter.

versions.text: And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter"—that noble price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew object is singular (אֹתוֹ, "it"), referring to the sum of money rather than the individual coins; rendering it as "the money" keeps the sense and avoids the pronoun shift, and "shekels" reflects the Hebrew measure more precisely than the vaguer "pieces."

versions.text: So I took the thirty shekels of silver and threw the money into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
versions.explanation: The first half of the verse is missing: the LORD's command "Throw it to the potter" and the ironic comment on the "noble price" at which they valued the shepherd. Without it the verse begins with "So I took..." with no antecedent command. The intentional changes from the earlier revision ("shekels" and "the money" for the singular object) are preserved.

text: Then I broke my second staff, Union, annulling the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
Then the LORD said to me: Take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

For I am raising up in the land a shepherd who will not care for the perishing, or seek the straying, or heal the injured, or feed the healthy, but will devour the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither away, and his right eye go utterly blind!
